rationale:
Issue 502 ("Potential Crash: HTTPBody.collect(upTo:) is not thread safe") is traced through merged PR #95 to fix commit 95307ba, whose head commit message states the fix returns a sequence throwing TooManyIterationsError instead of crashing. The retained minimized hunks are exactly that behavior change in Sources/OpenAPIRuntime/Interface/HTTPBody.swift: `makeAsyncIterator()` replaces `try! tryToMarkIteratorCreated()` with a do/catch that returns `.init(throwing: error)`, plus the new `fileprivate init(throwing:)` on AsyncIterator that the catch branch requires. No refactor, feature, config, or test-only content is in the minimized production patch; the two added doc lines are inline documentation of the changed declarations, not a standalone documentation change. The trigger extends the pre-existing Test_HTTPBody.testIterationBehavior_single with `for try await _ in body {}` after the body was already consumed, using AsyncSequence conformance that exists on the buggy revision (no fix-only symbol), so the same trigger source compiles on both revisions; on buggy the `try!` traps, on fixed the iterator throws and the catch block passes. Strict evidence records build.both_versions PASS, trigger.buggy_differential reproducing Test_HTTPBody.swift::testIterationBehavior_single, trigger.fixed_clean PASS, trigger.deterministic over 3 repetitions, full_suite.fixed_all_green, and post_minimization_validation PASS. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so no duplicate root cause.

Linked issue 502 ("Potential Crash: HTTPBody.collect(upTo:) is not thread safe", closed) and PR #95 commit b496acf ("return async sequence which throws TooManyIterationsError instead of crashing which fixes thread safety issue and potential crash in collect(upTo:)") describe one defect: HTTPBody.makeAsyncIterator used `try! tryToMarkIteratorCreated()`, so a second iteration attempt traps instead of surfacing an error, and the check-then-mark sequencing made that trap reachable from collect(upTo:) under concurrency. The minimized patch retains exactly the two semantic hunks that fix this: makeAsyncIterator now wraps tryToMarkIteratorCreated in do/catch and returns `.init(throwing: error)`, plus the new fileprivate `init(throwing:)` on AsyncIterator that the catch branch requires. The only non-code additions are the doc comments attached to those same two declarations; no refactor, feature extension, config, or test change is present in the minimized production patch (the dropped hunks were dead-code removal of the now-redundant checkIfCanCreateIterator and its call site). The trigger is a verbatim subset of the upstream test diff: appending `do { for try await _ in body {} ; XCTFail(...) } catch {}` to Test_HTTPBody.testIterationBehavior_single. It uses only API that already exists on the buggy revision (HTTPBody conforms to AsyncSequence there), so the same source builds on both revisions and the buggy failure is a genuine runtime trap from `try!`, not a missing-symbol compile error; the fixed revision throws and the test passes. Strict evidence for both the original and post-minimization runs reports all gates passed: build on both revisions, unique selector, buggy differential reproducing only Test_HTTPBody.swift::testIterationBehavior_single, deterministic over 3 repetitions across a 32-run matrix, fixed isolated/suite/reversed clean, and fixed full suite green. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so no duplicate root cause, and apple/swift-openapi-runtime#502 is the single allowed key.
